lead: The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) turns N numbers x[n] into N numbers X[k]. It is the DTFT sampled at ω = 2πk/N, so a computer can calculate a spectrum with finite arithmetic. The same finite sum is the Fourier-series analysis sum of the periodic extension of x[n]. The DFT is used in spectrum analysers, audio frames, OFDM in 4G and 5G, and any phone that runs a fast Fourier transform (FFT). This chapter defines the N-point DFT, its matrix form, circular operations, zero padding, Parseval and symmetry.
prereq: You need: Chapter 6.1, Chapter 6.2, and Unit 5 on discrete-time signals.

blocks.text: Let x[n] be a length-N sequence, n = 0, 1, ..., N−1. Define the twiddle factor W<sub>N</sub> = e<sup>−j2π/N</sup>. It is a point on the unit circle at angle −2π/N. The N-point DFT is the finite sum below. Equivalently, X[k] is the DTFS analysis sum of the periodic extension of x[n], with the 1/N factor moved to synthesis.

blocks.where: X[k] is the kth DFT value, k = 0, ..., N−1; x[n] is the input sequence; W<sub>N</sub> = e<sup>−j2π/N</sup> is the twiddle factor.

blocks.text: The inverse DFT returns x[n] from X[k]. The factor 1/N belongs to synthesis.

blocks.where: x[n] is the recovered sequence; X[k] is the DFT; 1/N is the synthesis scale factor.

blocks.text: For a length-N sequence, X[k] equals the DTFT X(e<sup>jω</sup>) at ω = 2πk/N. These are N equally spaced samples of one 2π period. The DFT is exact at those points; it says nothing between them.

In matrix form X = W x. The row k, column n entry of W is W<sub>N</sub><sup>nk</sup>. The inverse is x = (1/N) W<sup>H</sup> X, because W<sup>H</sup> W = N I. A computer therefore needs only a finite matrix-vector product.

sections.h3: Circular shift, circular convolution, zero padding

blocks.text: The DFT treats x[n] as one period of a periodic sequence of period N. A shift must wrap around. The index (n−m) mod N is a circular shift, not an ordinary delay.
y[n] = x[(n−m) mod N]  →  Y[k] = W<sub>N</sub><sup>km</sup> X[k]
blocks.where: m is an integer shift; mod N wraps indices into 0 to N−1; W<sub>N</sub> = e<sup>−j2π/N</sup>.

blocks.text: Circular convolution is defined next. Multiplication in the DFT domain gives circular convolution, because the sum wraps at N.
y[n] = Σ<sub>m=0</sub><sup>N−1</sup> x[m] h[(n−m) mod N]  →  Y[k] = X[k] H[k]
blocks.where: x[n] and h[n] both have length N; (n−m) mod N wraps the tail of h to the start; X[k] and H[k] are N-point DFTs.

blocks.text: Linear convolution of lengths N and M has length N+M−1. To get it from an L-point DFT, zero-pad both sequences to L ≥ N+M−1. For two length-N sequences, use L ≥ 2N−1. Without enough zeros, the tail wraps and adds to the start.

Zero padding to length L gives an L-point DFT, which is the DTFT of the original finite sequence sampled at L frequencies. More zeros give a finer frequency grid. They do not create new time information, and they do not improve true resolution set by the observation length.
Parseval for the DFT relates time-domain energy to DFT-bin energy.

blocks.where: |x[n]|² is the energy of sample n; |X[k]|² is the energy of bin k; N is the DFT length.

blocks.text: If x[n] is real, X[k] = X<sup>*</sup>[(-k) mod N]. Equivalently X[N−k] = X<sup>*</sup>[k] for k = 1, ..., N−1, and X[0] is real. Half the spectrum therefore carries the full information.

These symmetries explain why a real audio frame can be stored as about N/2+1 complex bins: the rest are conjugates. They also warn you that a peak in |X[k]| lies on the N-point grid; the true peak may lie between bins.

Fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithms compute the same X[k] with about N log₂ N operations instead of N². They change speed, not the definition. Spectrum analysers use DFT bins, OFDM in 4G and 5G uses inverse DFT to make subcarriers, and a phone computes FFTs on short audio frames.

figure.caption: The signal enters the DFT matrix and leaves as X[k]; the dashed return path is the inverse DFT, which needs the factor 1/N.

spec.title: The N-point DFT and back
spec.aria: Four blocks in a row with a return arrow: the signal enters the DFT matrix, produces X[k], and comes back through the inverse DFT.

examples.question: An N = 4 sequence is x[0] = 1, x[1] = 2, x[2] = 3, x[3] = 4. (a) Find X[k] for k = 0, 1, 2, 3 using W<sub>4</sub>. (b) Recover x[0] from the inverse DFT.
steps: N = 4 and W<sub>4</sub> = e<sup>−j2π/4</sup> = e<sup>−jπ/2</sup> = −j. Its powers are W<sub>4</sub><sup>0</sup> = 1, W<sub>4</sub><sup>1</sup> = −j, W<sub>4</sub><sup>2</sup> = −1, W<sub>4</sub><sup>3</sup> = j.
examples.check:
import cmath
x = [1, 2, 3, 4]
N = 4
X = []
for k in range(N):
    s = 0
    for n in range(N):
        s += x[n] * cmath.exp(-2j * cmath.pi * k * n / N)
    X.append(s)
vals = [X[0].real, X[1].real, X[1].imag, X[2].real, X[3].real, X[3].imag]
for v in vals:
    print(int(round(v, 10)))
x0 = sum(X) / N
print(int(round(x0.real, 10)))

traps: Using an N-point circular convolution when linear convolution is wanted. For two length-N sequences the linear result has length 2N−1; zero-pad to L ≥ 2N−1.
Forgetting the 1/N in synthesis or putting it in analysis. The standard DFT has no 1/N in analysis; the inverse has 1/N.
Treating X[k] as the continuous DTFT. X[k] is only N samples of X(e<sup>jω</sup>); zero padding adds samples, not new information.
Sign error in delay: x[(n−m) mod N] multiplies X[k] by W<sub>N</sub><sup>km</sup> = e<sup>−j2πkm/N</sup> for the standard DFT.
Assuming X[k] for real x[n] is all real. For real x[n], X[k] and X[N−k] are conjugates; only X[0] is always real.

quiz.q: Define W<sub>N</sub> and write the N-point DFT analysis sum.
quiz.a: W<sub>N</sub> = e<sup>−j2π/N</sup>. X[k] = Σ<sub>n=0</sub><sup>N−1</sup> x[n] W<sub>N</sub><sup>nk</sup> for k = 0, ..., N−1.

quiz.q: Why is the DFT called a sampled DTFT?
quiz.a: Because X[k] = X(e<sup>jω</sup>) at ω = 2πk/N. It evaluates the DTFT on N equally spaced points of one 2π period.

quiz.q: For N = 4 and x[n] = [1, 0, −1, 0], find X[k] for k = 0 to 3.
A real length-8 sequence has X[1] = 3 − 4j. Find X[7].
State DFT Parseval and its meaning in one sentence.
quiz.a: Σ |x[n]|² = (1/N) Σ |X[k]|². The energy in one period of the time sequence equals the energy in the N DFT bins divided by N.

quiz.q: Two length-4 sequences are circularly convolved with N = 4. Why may the result differ from linear convolution, and what length L avoids it?
quiz.a: The N-point sum wraps the tail of h to the start. Linear convolution has length 4+4−1 = 7, so use zero padding to L ≥ 7.

quiz.q: Zero padding a 64-sample audio frame to 1024 points does not improve true resolution. Why?
quiz.a: Zero padding only samples the DTFT of the same 64 samples more densely. It adds no new time data. True resolution is set by the 64-sample observation length and the window used.

beyond: Not for the exam. The FFT is a standard library call in Python, C and Java, and its radix-2 form is a common interview question. OFDM systems add a cyclic prefix after the inverse DFT so that circular convolution becomes linear convolution over the channel. Spectrum analysers trade window length against leakage, so they apply windows before the DFT. Search next for radix-2 FFT, OFDM cyclic prefix, spectral leakage and window functions.
